top_choice_rationale: P002 rewards one sharp, complete idea, the magic-wavelength optical lattice that cancels the clock-transition light shift so many atoms can be interrogated at once, realised in Sr and Yb and reproduced and compared across several countries at about 10^-18. The credit to Katori and Ye is the cleanest on the slate and the citation can stay on invention and realisation. The overlap with the 2005 and 2012 prizes is a difference of degree, since the lattice clock solves a different problem. I rank P001 second because its prediction and observation are well matched, but the pairing mechanism is open, the field is eight years old and Cao is outside the credit. P004 is third because of the 2012 overlap and the Monroe and Wineland-lineage credit. P003 is fourth because Bernevig-Hughes-Zhang and Hasan are omitted and the 2016 topology prize is nearby.
recusal_note: none apparent from profile; I work in neighbouring atomic theory and have no documented collaboration with Katori, Ye or the other credited names, though I have collaborated with L'Huillier's group and others on attosecond physics, which is not part of any proposal
